qs.q:
Language Teachers — Which person had a language teacher who…

A=Aaron (French teacher taught entirely in French, even beginners, came Saturdays, Aaron became fluent)
B=Brigitte (English teacher: positive feedback, subtle corrections, varied methods, word dominos/charades as rewards)
C=Carl (Spanish teacher: fun methods, pirate dress-up, treasure hunt, abandoned classroom, then went abroad)
D=Daphne (Russian teacher: personal, joined games, sat with groups, visits/excursions, never native language in class)
E=Ella (Italian teacher from university, wanted success but confusing worksheets, students dozed off, gave sweets for book reports)
F=Frank (German teacher, former sociologist, focused on mistakes not progress, made him hate German)

0. took part in games? [D=Daphne]
1. taught another subject at their school?
2. never spoke their native language in class?
3. preferred traditional teaching methods?
4. enjoyed teaching grammar?
5. introduced games as a reward?
6. organised extra lessons for them?
7. encouraged them to read literature?
8. concentrated on correcting errors?
9. took them on field trips?
10. taught them to speak fluently?
11. had no previous teaching experience?
12. left to teach abroad?
items: 1 — taught another subject at their school?
2 — never spoke their native language in class?

"I think HER PERFORMANCE STANDS ABOVE that of the other nominees, and I would be DISAPPOINTED if she didn't win."

opts: is sure to win an Oscar.

"The golden statuette has to be seen as a REWARD FOR ARTISTIC VALUE, otherwise it has little meaning."

opts: to provide awards for the in-crowd.

Write an essay of 200–250 words.
Your essay must have an introduction, body and conclusion.

"Some people think that spending lengthy periods away from home helps young people develop. Others disagree."

Discuss both of these views and give your own opinion.

You will hear five people talking about doing sport.
Match the speakers 1–5 with what each person thinks about doing sport.
Do not use any letter more than once. There are three letters you do not need.

A — It's a waste of time.
B — It gives you confidence.
C — It prepares you for life.
D — It wins you friends.
E — It's unhealthy.
F — It's expensive.
G — It keeps you fit.
H — It gives a sense of purpose.
rights: A — It's a waste of time.
C — It prepares you for life.
